answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce token for a fixed period before it may earn reputation or claim work. Rewards accrue only to identities that complete verifiable tasks, while a slashable bond is forfeited for proven fraud. This does not make sybils impossible: an attacker can still create many identities, but must tie up capital in every one and risk losing it. The raven may cross a dune in a spiral, but each false identity still pays its own bond.
